references.text: God commanded Moses to establish cities of refuge for anyone who kills someone accidentally, without intent. This expands on the promise in Exodus regarding a place of refuge.
Describes the criteria for unintentional killing and how the assembly is to judge between the killer and the avenger of blood, relating to one who had no prior enmity.
Moses set aside three cities of refuge east of the Jordan for anyone who kills their neighbor accidentally and without previous hostility.
Detailed instructions about the cities of refuge in the Promised Land for someone who strikes another down unintentionally, so that innocent blood is not shed.
Gives a concrete example of unintentional killing and explains the purpose of the place of refuge to protect one who had no hatred toward their neighbor beforehand.
Joshua appointed the cities of refuge as fulfillment of what God promised through Moses—a place to flee for anyone who kills someone by accident.
Hannah confesses that the LORD puts to death and gives life, that He brings down to Sheol and raises up again—God governs the circumstances of life and death.
Proverbs teaches that lots are cast into the lap, but the decision comes from the LORD—God directs the events in people's lives.
Many plans are in a man's heart, but the counsel of the LORD will stand—God is the one who causes events to happen according to His will.
Direct interpretation of the law: Joshua 20:3 implements the law concerning cities of refuge introduced in Exodus 21:13.
Restatement of the laws: Deuteronomy 4:42 confirms and expands on the conditions for refuge as established in Exodus 21:13.
